title: Reduce parse fanout and add ingress coalescer + session memoization for prompt preprocessing
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
We observe high per-request overhead in the prefill/ingest side of the runtime due to excessive parser fanout (same incoming prompt routed through multiple tokenizer/normalizer lanes) and repeated work at session granularity. This ticket implements an ingress coalescer and session memoization layer plus a lightweight 'mono-token cheap-path' to cut CPU cycles and latency for common short prompts.

Problem details:
- Production traces show median prefill CPU spend ~14ms and p99 ~120ms for prompt preprocessing on busy hosts. A large fraction of that time is scheduling + duplicate parse work when the same session or near-duplicate prefixes arrive concurrently.
- Parser fanout arises from per-request lane selection that doesn't dedupe at the TCP/ingest boundary; downstream tokenizer stages end up doing identical normalization for requests in the same session or with the same short prefix.
- Short prompts (<= 6 tokens after normalization) are extremely latency-sensitive and should avoid heavyweight pipeline stages.

Goals / success metrics:
- Reduce median prefill CPU time by >= 25% on synthetics representing our 'chatty' workload.
- Reduce p99 prefill latency by >= 20% for requests with session affinity.
- Improve overall throughput on small-payload workloads by 12-18% on GPU-backed serving nodes.
- No regression in correctness: normalized tokens must match existing canonical lexer output 1:1.

Design / Approach:
1) Ingress coalescer (front-line): group concurrent requests sharing session_id or identical prefix hash within 5ms windows. Coalescer returns a single normalized token stream to downstream lanes and fans out only the normalized result. This reduces duplicate parse runs.
2) Session memo table: small in-memory LRU per-host keyed by (session_id, prefix_hash) with TTL 30s; stores normalized token arrays and metadata (length, hash). Memo table is hit-before-parse in the ingest path. Size is tunable (default 16k entries).
3) Mono-token cheap-path: a fast path specialized for normalized outputs with <=6 tokens that bypasses normalization reflow, heavy Unicode NFKC transforms, and token-mapping tables. It relies on a verified subset of ascii/utf8 and falls back to full pipeline on mismatch.
4) Kernel hinting for downstream lanes: when the ingress coalescer produces a normalized sequence it attaches a lightweight kernel_hint header for the runtime scheduler to prefer small-sequence kernels and packed KV-cache placement (reduces decode-side kernel switching).
5) Observability: add per-request tags in traces for coalescer_hit, memo_hit, cheap_path_taken, and add Grafana panels with hit rates and latency deltas.

Implementation plan and milestones:
- Spike (3d): implement prototype coalescer + microbench harness. Produce a baseline set of microbench numbers and an invariants test to ensure canonical output equality.
- Prototype (5d): integrate memo table with eviction policy, implement cheap-path, add kernel_hint header. End-to-end bench against synthetic chatty workload and internal replay logs.
- Review & harden (4d): safety checks, fallback correctness, and add telemetry. Add unit tests for edge-case encodings.
- Canary (2w): roll out to 10% of serving fleet using canary rollout with A/B metrics (RT, CPU, error rate).
- Ramp (1w): increase to 50% then 100% if metrics are green.

Bench Plan / Expected numbers (from local runs):
- Synthetic 1k rps of short prompts: median prefill CPU cycles down 27%, p99 reduced 24%.
- End-to-end throughput: +15% improvement on small-payload mixes.
- Memo table hit-rate target: 40-60% on chatty sessions, adjustable via TTL.

Testing & Validation:
- Golden canonicalization tests comparing normalized token arrays against current production lexer for 10k seed prompts (from internal corpus).
- Property tests for cheap-path: ensure identical decode tokenization for validated subset; automatic fallback on mismatch.
- Chaos test: force memo table evictions and coalescer de-synchronization to validate fallbacks.
- Load test: run replay of last week's customer traffic on canary cluster and compare.

Rollout and Monitoring:
- Add Alert: cheap_path_mismatch_rate > 0.1% for 10m -> auto rollback.
- Dashboard panels: coalescer latency, memo hit rate, cheap-path taken %, per-host CPU reduction delta.
- Canary evaluation runbook: 24h green window required for full ramp; rollback if CPU or error rate regresses by >5% from baseline.

Risks and mitigations:
- Incorrect normalization divergence: mitigate with extensive golden tests and conservative fallback to full pipeline on any mismatch.
- Memory pressure from memo table: defaults tuned low and LRU eviction; host-level memory ceiling enforced.
- Increased scheduling latency from coalescer windows: keep coalescing window <=5ms and allow immediate passthrough for latency-critical flags.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- TTL sizing: shorter TTL reduces correctness staleness but lowers hit rates. Will experiment with 10s/30s/60s in canaries.
- Coalescing window: 1ms vs 5ms trade between hit-rate and added ingress latency.
- Cheap-path whitelist: how broad can ascii/utf8 subset be before correctness risk grows? Start narrow and broaden if stable.
